claims.text: A nanoscale heterogeneous microstructure of interconnected magnetically soft clusters in a stiffer, weakly magnetic matrix enables a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
Rapid local reorientation of magnetic moments produces a large magnetic entropy change.
The interconnected heterogeneous architecture supports efficient heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability.
The conventionally melted and cast starting alloy is predominantly single-phase and lacks controlled phase heterogeneity.
The starting alloy has the potential for nanoscale segregation of Fe, Mn, Co, Ni, or Cr.
Controlled annealing and/or thermomechanical deformation can induce and refine nanoscale phase separation into magnetically soft clusters and a weakly magnetic continuous matrix.
Large, reversible rotation of localized magnetic moments occurs within the soft clusters under low applied fields.
Reversible moment rotation in the soft clusters leads to significant magnetic entropy change.
The interconnected matrix facilitates rapid thermal conduction.
The interconnected matrix distributes strain, reduces magnetocaloric-cycle hysteresis, and maintains mechanical stability.
Processing that creates the proposed heterogeneity will enhance low-field magnetic entropy change relative to the as-cast alloy, potentially by approximately twofold or more.
The processed alloy will retain or improve heat-exchange rates while maintaining low magnetic hysteresis.
The processing will not degrade quasi-static mechanical properties.
The as-cast, single-phase or minimally segregated baseline has a modest low-field magnetocaloric effect.
The proposed mechanism should apply near room temperature, below approximately 1 T, when the induced heterogeneity is tens to a few hundred nanometers in scale.
Excessively large phases may trigger first-order transitions with significant hysteresis or compromise mechanical integrity.
